title: Advocates, traders protest in Vaniyambadi for additional district court

ai.summary: Advocates and traders in Vaniyambadi staged a protest demanding an additional district court and permanent building for the existing court complex due to monsoon risks and poor court infrastructure.

facts.claim: Advocates and traders staged a protest near a bus terminus in Vaniyambadi town on Thursday
facts.quote: Advocates, traders and residents staged a protest near a bus terminus in Vaniyambadi town on Thursday, demanding an additional district court and a permanent building for the court complex.

facts.claim: The protest was held in the wake of the onset of the Northeast monsoon
facts.quote: The protest was held in the wake of the onset of the Northeast monsoon, when it could be risky to conduct court proceedings at the dilapidated Judicial Magistrate court.

facts.claim: A.C. Devakumar, president of Bar Association (Vaniyambadi), said work to build a permanent court complex should be expedited and an additional district court should be set up
facts.quote: ‘Work to build a permanent court complex should be expedited. An additional district court should also be set up in the court complex’, said A.C. Devakumar, president, Bar Association (Vaniyambadi).

facts.claim: Vaniyambadi has three lower courts located in different areas, each at least 1.5 km apart
facts.quote: At present, Vaniyambadi has three lower courts that are located in different areas in the town. Each court, on an average, is located at least 1.5 km away from the other court.

facts.claim: Each court handles over 100 cases daily with 1,500-2,000 pending cases
facts.quote: On an average, over 100 cases come up at each court every day. Currently, 1,500 - 2,000 cases are pending before each of these three courts.

facts.claim: Case bundles and court records get damaged during monsoon due to flooding
facts.quote: Case bundles and court records get damaged during monsoon as the building is inundated.

ai.background_note: Vaniyambadi town in Tamil Nadu has three lower courts with poor infrastructure, leading to monsoon-related risks and long wait times for litigants.
